ariyipp links two phones over end-to-end encrypted FCM to relay SMS between them: a companion phone (with the SIM) forwards its incoming SMS to your main device, where you read and reply to them as a chat, and the main device can send SMS back through the companion. The main device can also show the companion\'s battery and signal, and track bills and parking from your messages with the optional Reminders module. Notification capture and webhook posting are optional extras. This device\'s role is shown below, and can be switched anytime.

ariyipp v1.7 - Your history is safer: the database key no longer depends on the settings store, a passing storage error no longer sets the history aside, and a restore is all or nothing (and tells the companion where to find this phone). Fixes to v1.6: two cards due the same day stay two bills; refused-send and webhook notices no longer replace each other; the key-mismatch alert no longer repeats; commands from a restored or out-of-order Main go through; a catch-up no longer interrupts a repush. Relay: identical repeat SMS are both kept; the first SMS after a remote webhook enable isn't skipped; a phone with heartbeat off says so instead of looking unreachable; inline replies no longer time out; notifications no longer replace each other after a restart; a new Firebase file offers a restart. Reminders: Skip next skips one bill, not a whole burst; parking apps' ongoing notifications are read; a badly written pattern can no longer stall the scan (and the editor refuses one); amounts like 1.234.567 parse; Mark paid leaves already-settled bills alone. Screens: rotating keeps your edits and no longer leaves an empty backup file; Save works once per tap; deleting a message asks first; chat no longer jumps while scrolling up. Faster start, fewer wakeups on the companion, and a smaller download (6.2 MB).

ariyipp v1.6 - Update BOTH phones: this version won't exchange messages with an older one, and says so if the other phone needs updating. Safer: the database is now encrypted on the phone; the pairing and backup screens are protected from screenshots (Settings > Privacy, where messages can be protected too); the companion has a Security screen with send limits (20 an hour, 50 a day by default) and an optional "only numbers that texted me" list; backup passphrases need 16+ characters without repeats or runs; copied messages are marked sensitive. More reliable relay: switching a phone to Main stops it relaying; a long outage no longer loses SMS (Main asks for a catch-up); a bad token holds SMS instead of dropping them; webhook redirects aren't followed; n8n's default reply counts as delivered (you're told once); a refused or late command shows why on its bubble; double-tapping Send sends one SMS; a regenerated key is saved at once. Reminders: a re-sent reminder no longer makes a second bill; Calculate now keeps your corrections and doesn't revive ended parking; month-end bills keep their day; paying late doesn't skip the next cycle; dates like 7 Feb 2026, 5/1/2027 and 2:30 pm are understood; due dates stay put after a time-zone change; a late parking reminder still rings.

ariyipp v1.5 - The Reminders total is no longer always in AED. It is shown in your default currency, which follows your phone's region (from the SIM, then the network, then the language setting) unless you choose one under Reminders settings - type a code like INR, or Rs, ₹, Dhs or $. Clear the field to go back to automatic; the line under it says what automatic currently picks. Exchange rates are fetched for whichever currency you use, and a bill without a currency counts as being in it. Your choice is kept in backups.

ariyipp v1.4 - The biggest update yet.

Reminders (new, optional - turn it on in Settings): ariyipp can now track bill due dates and parking expiry from the SMS and notifications it already sees, in a new Reminders tab. Long-press a message and choose Create reminder rule: the sender and every field are drafted for you by an auto-parser you can override, or select the amount or date in the sample to build the pattern without writing any regex. Rules run the moment a matching SMS or notification arrives. Bills remind you ahead at a time you choose; parking sessions extend themselves on renewal and ring an alarm before they run out. A bill can be marked paid automatically when the bank's payment confirmation arrives - optionally only if the amount matches - and that works for bills you add by hand too. Manual bills repeat every N days, weeks, months or years, with notes, categories and their own reminder lead. One figure shows everything due in the next 30 days in AED, converted at daily exchange rates (fetched once a day from open.er-api.com; nothing about you or your bills is sent). A Compact view fits one entry per line.

Companion status: while the main device's Status screen is open, it shows the companion's battery, signal, network and VPN as live gauges, and the companion can alert you when its battery runs low or its wifi has been down too long.

More reliable: no more false "isn't responding" alerts - the phone asks the other one to answer before warning. A broken relay setup holds an SMS and retries instead of dropping it. Push tokens heal themselves when they change, and Relay has a Get a new push token button. Chat history has its own setting and is kept forever by default; a repush or catch-up is stored quietly instead of buzzing once per message.

A new look: colours rebuilt so all text meets WCAG AA contrast in light, dark and AMOLED; calmer motion; a Status screen of clear rows and badges; tappable links in chat; and a download about a fifth smaller.

Also: backups now include your reminder rules, bills and every setting; Do Not Disturb bypass for alarms in one tap; settings save as you change them; Back twice to exit keeps your place.

New permissions, all for Reminders and companion status: exact alarms, full-screen alarm, vibrate, set alarm and Do Not Disturb access on the main device; network and wifi state on the companion.

ariyipp v1.3 - Security hardening. Webhook URLs must now be https: a plain http:// address is rejected when you save it and blocked before any upload, and the same check now applies to a webhook config pushed from the main device. The companion also shows a notification whenever the main device changes its webhook settings, so a remote change is never silent, and accepting pushed config is now opt-in (off by default). Encrypted backups use stronger key derivation (600,000 PBKDF2 iterations, up from 120,000) and require a 12-character passphrase; older backups still restore with their original passphrase. Notification capture gained guardrails against a misbehaving or hostile app flooding local storage: a per-field length cap, a per-app rate limit, and an overall pending-row ceiling.

ariyipp v1.2 - Messages: long-press a message to share it to any other installed app (separate from Forward, which relays it as a new SMS through the companion); the chat screen's own menu now has Mute/Unmute and Mark as read too. The Messages list gets a collapsible search bar and a new overflow menu with Mark all as read and multi-select (Select all/Deselect all, Mark as read, Mute, Delete) - long-press a conversation's avatar to jump straight into selection. Predictive back gesture support throughout the app. Status and Messages no longer visibly pop in their content a beat after the tab-switch animation finishes, and Status stops re-checking permissions on every tab switch. Fixed dark mode showing near-black on the chat screen and inside Settings sub-screens, and an overflow menu that blended into its own background; fixed low-contrast incoming message bubbles (plus the date header and compose field) in light mode. Also fixed a couple of smaller Messages-list glitches: a jarring jump when opening/closing search, and the list briefly appearing empty right after.

ariyipp v1.1 - Chat screen redesign: compact bubbles with an inline timestamp, a floating date header, and a jump-to-latest button, grouped by day. Delivery-receipt ticks on sent messages are now real (received by companion / handed to SIM / carrier-confirmed) instead of decorative. Performance pass: chats open by loading only the newest history page, the conversation list updates itself live instead of polling, relayed payloads are smaller over the air, long SMS split reliably, connections are reused instead of re-authenticating on every send, cold start skips crypto work off the main thread, chat history respects a retention setting, and the conversation list/search now stay fast via a dedicated index as history grows. Also a batch of UI bug fixes: bubble line spacing, RTL timestamp placement, a shared-background flicker, and an oversized corner-radius clamp on short messages.

ariyipp v1.0 - Pair two phones over end-to-end encrypted FCM to relay SMS between them. The main device receives the relayed SMS as a searchable chat and can reply; the companion phone (with the SIM) forwards its incoming SMS and sends SMS on request. Pick a role on first run and switch anytime. Optional extras: notification capture to a webhook, encrypted backup and restore, per-conversation mute, and a liveness heartbeat that warns if the other device goes offline. Bring your own Firebase project (BYO-FCM).
1. Tap “Grant notification access” and enable ariyipp in the system list - this lets the app see notifications.\n2. Tap “Ignore battery optimization” so it runs reliably in the background.

Enter your Webhook URL and the auth token. The token is sent as a header: by default “Authorization: Bearer <token>”. For a custom Header Auth credential, set the Auth header name to “key” and clear the prefix so the raw token is sent. Tap the eye icon to reveal the token. Use an https URL - content is sensitive.
Under “Included apps”, tap “Choose apps” to pick which apps to capture. If you select none, all apps are captured. Selecting apps limits capture to just those.

Settings → “Keywords & notes” lists every app you selected under Apps. Against each app you can set:

• Keywords - a comma-separated list, e.g. “delivered, out for delivery”. Only notifications containing one of them (in the title, text or subtext, case-insensitive) are logged. Leave it empty to log every notification from that app.

• Notes - optional free text appended, on a new line, to the logged notification's text field. Useful for tagging a source, e.g. “work phone”. Notes are added even in metadata-only mode, since you wrote them yourself.

Excluded keywords under Privacy still win: a notification matching one is dropped regardless of these rules.
Some apps re-post the same notification repeatedly. “Ignore duplicate window” drops identical content from the same app seen within that many seconds (default one day). Set 0 to keep every copy.
Choose when uploads run: Periodic (every N minutes, min 15), Threshold (after N pending), or Manual (“Sync now” only). Optionally restrict to Wi-Fi or to charging to save battery/data.

Turn off “Capture notification body” to store metadata only. Add excluded keywords to drop notifications containing sensitive words (e.g. OTP). “Keep notification records” controls how long captured notification rows are kept before purging; it never touches chat history, which has its own setting on the Relay screen (forever by default).

• 403 on upload: the auth header/token is wrong - for custom Header Auth use header name “key” and an empty prefix.\n• Nothing captured: grant notification access; check your included-apps selection.\n• Uploads delayed: allow the app to ignore battery optimization, or use “Sync now”.

This app is sideloaded and asks for SMS permissions on the companion, so Google Play Protect will warn on install and on some updates - that’s expected, not a sign of malware.

• On the prompt, tap “More details”, then “Install anyway”.
• If an update is blocked outright with a conflict error, that’s a signing mismatch, not Play Protect - uninstall the old build first (you’ll re-pair), then install the new one.
• On your own devices you can make updates apply silently over ADB (no fingerprint needed):
 adb shell settings put global verifier_verify_adb_installs 0
 adb install -r ariyipp.apk
